sentences.text: Vegavis iaai is an extinct bird belonging to the family Vegaviidae and stands as the sole known member of its genus.
This species is most closely related to the modern family Anatidae, which includes ducks and geese, though it is not viewed as a direct ancestor of that group.
Taxonomically, Vegavis belongs to the parent group Anseriformes.
The type specimen, cataloged as MLP 93-I-3-1, was discovered in deposits at Cape Lamb on Vega Island, Antarctica, in 1992.
Formal description did not occur until 2005 because the fossil consists of delicate remains embedded in a concretion that required meticulous preparation.
Scientists utilized computed axial tomography scans to study the bone structure without risking damage or destruction of the fragile fossils.
While Irazoqui and colleagues initially described the taxon, it was formally recognized as a new species in 2026.
The type locality for this species is the López de Bertodano Formation.
The specific name 'notopothousa' combines Greek words meaning 'south' and 'longing', referencing the fossil's discovery in the Southern Hemisphere and its current housing in the Northern Hemisphere.
Vegavis possessed a high metabolism that enabled it to survive in the high latitudes of Antarctica.
The species exhibits osteosclerosis, a condition potentially linked to variations in diving behavior.

Vegavis notopothousa lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian stage, in Antarctica. The geological unit containing fossils is dated to approximately 69.2 million years ago, while the genus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the same stage.
